newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk finishes share transfer to workers.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk finishes share transfer to workers.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel has finished distributing 10 percent of its shares to company employees in line with its privatisation programme, the company said in a statement on Thursday.

Over 12.5 million shares held in a special fund set up for employees have now been transferred to workers. Around 1.5 million shares, each with a nominal value of 250 roubles, were distributed for free, and the rest were sold to employees at 5,361 roubles per share, Norilsk said.
Norilsk shares traded at $4.72 on the Russian Trading System at around 11:50 a.m. (0850 GMT), down from Wednesday's close of $5.40.
Norilsk said the shares were divided up among 150,000 employees, or around half the company's total workforce, in line with agreements with trade union committees and privatisation officials.
Norilsk said workers had full rights to trade the shares from April 8.
The share distribution scheme was agreed between the State Property Fund and RAO Norilsky Nikel in November 1996.
Commercial bank Uneximbank controls 38 percent, or 51 percent of voting shares, in the Norilsk group, one of the world's leading producers of nickel and platinum group metals.
